clean_statement:
Let $k$ have characteristic zero and let $\mathfrak a\subseteq k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ be a binomial ideal containing no monomial, with minimal binomial generators $f_i=x^{a_i}-\gamma_i x^{b_i}$ for $1\leq i\leq r$. Put $$A= egin{pmatrix}a_1&\cdots&a_r&b_1&\cdots&b_r\ I_r&I_r\end{pmatrix}$$ and maximize $\sum_{i=1}^r(\mu_i+
u_i)$ subject to $A(\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_r,
u_1,\ldots,
u_r)^{\mathsf T}\leq\mathbf1$ and $\mu_i,
u_i\in\mathbb Q_{\geq0}$. Must there exist an optimal solution $(\mu,
u)$ whose image $A(\mu,
u)^{\mathsf T}$ differs from the image of every other optimal solution?

original_statement:
Let \mathfrak{a}\subseteq k[x_{1},\ldots,x_{n}] be a binomial ideal containing no monomials, and let f_{1},\ldots,f_{r} be a minimal binomial generating system. In the linear program of Proposition 5, formed from the exponent vectors of the generators, does there always exist an optimal rational solution (\mu,
u) whose image A(\mu,
u) is distinct from A(\mu',
u') for every other optimal solution (\mu',
u')?
